clips.title: Simpler frontend
clips.prompt: Show the old and current screens and explain what you wanted to make easier.
clips.script:
The first version of BUY HARD had a lot going on.

I liked the pieces, but I kept asking: what should someone look at first?

So I’ve been simplifying it. Fewer panels. A clearer buying decision. And the buyer close by when you need it.

These are the old and current sample screens.

Curious which version feels easier to you.
clips.edit: Real founder opening → archived UI → current sample → keep it simple → buyer conversation → founder closing. 38 seconds; actual voice and lime captions.
clips.fallback: The original two-image version is preserved in the earlier campaign receipt; the video is now saved in this slot.

clips.title: Sales into supplies · optional
clips.prompt: Explain the coffee-sales example to a café operator.
clips.script:
Here’s an idea I’m exploring for BUY HARD.

If you sell more takeaway coffees, you use more cups and lids. That should help plan the next supply order.

This animation shows the idea with sample data. The goal is to connect sales to the buying work.

Which sales or inventory app would this need to work with in your business?

clips.title: More of this work
clips.targetKind: Original slot held as draft; reschedule only after matching video
clips.prompt: Tell a potential collaborator which parts of building BUY HARD you have enjoyed.
clips.script:
I’ve really enjoyed building BUY HARD.

Figuring out the problem, making the interface feel simpler, and connecting the buyer to the tools it needs.

I’ve enjoyed the small details too, like making the buying decision clear and leaving room for a different answer.

I’d love to do more of this. If your team is building useful AI products, say hi.

clips.title: What would you hand off?
clips.targetKind: Original slot held as draft; reschedule only after matching video
clips.prompt: Share the ambition and invite a real purchasing story.
clips.script:
What if the everyday supplies for a business just stayed stocked?

That’s the idea I’m exploring with BUY HARD.

I’m starting with the repeat purchases: cups, gloves, labels. The things you need again and again, but probably don’t want to keep thinking about.

If you’ve dealt with buying at work, what’s the first part you’d happily hand off?
